2. The case of the plaintiff-respondents was that one Kalu was the owner of the suit plots which he transferred to Joynal Ali Munshi predecessor-in- interest of the plaintiff-respondents by a registered sale deed dated 15.6.1907 and delivered possession. Joynal Ali Munshi had been in possession. He was not educated and therefore entrusted his brother Joynul Abedin for recording the suit land at the time of settlement operation but the said Joynul Abedin got 8 annas share recorded in ills name Joynul Abedin did not claim the suit find even after the death of Joynal Ali Munshi. The plaintiffs had been possessing the suit land and were not aware about the wrong record of the suit land. Their father died after the war of liberation and the plaintiffs were still minor at the time. Since the record was wrongly made in the name of Joynul Abedin he filed the suit for declaration of title. The defendant contested the suit. Their case was that Joynal Ali Munshi and Joynal Abedin were full brothers and they used to reside in the same house. Joynal Ali Munshi being the elder brother used to look after the family and the suit land was purchased in the name of Joynal Ali Munshi alone. When the matter came to light Joynal Abedin recorded 8 annas share in his name in R.S. and S.A. Khatian. After the death of Joynal Abedin the disputed land was possessed by the defendants and they also paid rents. On examination of witnesses and on consideration of the facts and circumstances the Assistant Judge decreed the suit. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 preferred the aforementioned title appeal and the learned  Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court and allowed the appeal. 

 3. The High Court Division heard the matter in revision. It appeared to the High Court Division that the appellate court presumed that since the two brothers Joynal Ali Munshi and Joynal Abedin used to live on the same family fund therefore both the brothers were equally entitled to get 8 annas share each of the suit land and therefore Joynal Abedin the predecessors of the defendant-petitioners got his name recorded in R.S. and S.A. Khatians. However it was seen that the trial court had found that the plaintiffs had proved that the suit property was in possession of the plaintiffs and the same was recorded wrongly in the name of Joynal Abedin; the defendants could not prove their possession and further the defendant-petitioners also failed to prove that the consideration money was paid from the common fund of the family. There was not a single witness examined to prove that consideration money was paid from the common fund of the family. Further it was found Joynal Abedin had no any income or source of income to pay the consideration money of the Kabala in the year 1907. In support of the plaintiff-respondents case before the High Court Division the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents relied on a decision in the case of Farrokh Ahmed Vs. Abul Khair and others reported in VI DLR page 365 in which it was held that "purchase of property by a Muslim in his own name raises no presumption that he acquired it for himself and for other members of the family with whom he may be living jointly. Muslim family law does not recognize joint family system. The rules applicable to the members of a joint family do not apply to the members of the Muslim family." The trial court also observed that payment of consideration money is the most important matter with regard to the ownership of the property. It was on record that defendant-petitioners examined no witness to prove that the consideration money came from the common fund of the joint family. In the absence of legal evidence that the consideration money was paid out of the fund of the joint family, joint-ownership could not be claimed. The High Court Division rightly observed that if the consideration money flowed from the source of income of the joint family the case might have been otherwise but since the defendant-petitioners failed to prove that the consideration money was paid from the common fund of the joint family their claim does not sustain.
